items.question: Someone is underperforming and someone else is needed. Which decision do you take faster?
items.subject_said: I have never regretted firing someone slowly, only hiring someone quickly

items.question: There is budget for a role nobody is currently doing. Do you open it?
items.subject_said: I am inventing a job to justify a feeling

items.question: Two suppliers, one cheaper, one candid about problems. Which do you pay?
items.subject_said: I will pay more for a supplier who tells me bad news early

items.question: A new supplier says their last contract had no issues. What now?
items.subject_said: if the answer is nothing I stop there

items.question: Demand is forecast to double next quarter. Do you hire now?
items.subject_said: I will not hire ahead of demand

items.question: What has to be in front of you before a meeting is worth taking?
items.subject_said: I do not take a meeting without the previous quarter's numbers in front of me

items.question: What evidence do you want before opening a role?
items.subject_said: whether the work existed last quarter and somebody was doing it badly

items.question: How do you know six months later whether a hire worked?
items.subject_said: I write down the one number that will tell me in six months whether it worked

items.question: A deal is stuck. What is the first thing you ask?
items.subject_said: how long it has been stalled

items.question: Someone brings you a plan. Where do you look first?
items.subject_said: I look for the step that has never been done before

items.question: What is your first question to a new supplier?
items.subject_said: what went wrong on their last contract

items.question: When in a supplier conversation do you talk about price?
items.subject_said: Price negotiations come after that, never before
